topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how local treatments remove or destroy tumours and why their success depends on tumour location and spread.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how cytotoxic drugs kill cancer cells and why their effectiveness is constrained by toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how blocking required hormonal signals suppresses the growth of hormone-dependent cancer cells.

topics.label: Exploiting cell cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing checkpoint proteins create vulnerabilities that can be exploited to selectively destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how PARP inhibition exploits defective BRCA-mediated DNA repair to produce selective cancer cell death.

topics.label: Oncogene-directed therapy and kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying cancer-driving oncogenes and inhibiting their activity with targeted drugs.

topics.label: Resistance and limitations of kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often provides continuing disease management rather than a durable cure.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeting of cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognising cancer-cell surface proteins can direct therapeutic effects towards those cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This material evaluates whether the body's existing immune responses provide protection against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade restores antitumour T-cell responses and why tumour neoantigens influence treatment success.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic approaches that give T cells a specified tumour target rather than relying on naturally occurring recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and personalised strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This material considers how treatment selection can be improved despite variable patient responses and the adaptability of cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This material assesses improvements in cancer outcomes while distinguishing treatment effects from changes in prevention and detection.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how to pursue better cancer treatments while weighing their uncertain benefits against established outcomes and patients' quality of life.
